title: Reddivaripalli — Our Heritage
lede: A living record of unity, leadership, agriculture, faith, and the people who shaped our village — preserved for every generation.

history.title: Our History
paragraphs: Reddivaripalli, originally known as Kondareddigaripalli, traces its origins to the mid-19th century (around 1850). The village was founded by the visionary Sri G. Konda Reddy of the Gundluru family, whose leadership, wisdom, and dedication laid the foundation for a united and prosperous community.
As time passed, Kondareddigaripalli gradually came to be known as Reddivaripalli, the name by which it is proudly recognized today.

For generations, Reddivaripalli served as one of the most respected villages in the region. More than 32 surrounding villages looked to Reddivaripalli for leadership, guidance, and the resolution of community matters. It became a central place where people gathered to seek advice, settle disputes, and strengthen relationships between neighboring villages.

Sri G. Konda Reddy was admired not only as the founder of the village but also as a wise and compassionate leader. He believed that every individual should be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of caste, religion, or social background. His home was always open to visitors, and it became a tradition that no guest would ever leave the village without being offered food, hospitality, and assistance.

Under his leadership, Reddivaripalli became known for its unity, generosity, and strong sense of community. He encouraged agriculture, promoted education, preserved cultural traditions, and introduced village-wide celebrations that brought everyone together as one family.

One of his most remarkable contributions was Vana Pandaga, during which the entire village gathered together for two days to pray for timely rains, prepare traditional food, celebrate as one community, and seek blessings for a prosperous agricultural season.

After Sri G. Konda Reddy, Sri G. Venkata Subba Reddy continued this remarkable legacy. As the respected village head and Panchayat leader, he earned the trust and admiration of people not only from Reddivaripalli but also from the surrounding villages. Political leaders, government officials, and respected elders regularly visited Reddivaripalli to seek his guidance and participate in Panchayat discussions. His wisdom, fairness, and impartial judgments helped resolve disputes peacefully.

Today, more than 170 years later, Reddivaripalli continues to preserve the values established by its founders — unity, justice, hospitality, agriculture, culture, devotion, education, and service to society.

agriculture.title: Agriculture — The Heart of Reddivaripalli
agriculture.lede: Agriculture has always been the backbone of Reddivaripalli and the primary source of livelihood for many families. Blessed with fertile soil, favorable climate, and the dedication of hardworking farmers, the village has prospered through agriculture for generations.
agriculture.closing: Agriculture is more than an occupation in Reddivaripalli — it is a way of life. Every harvest reflects the dedication, resilience, and hard work of our farmers. Their efforts not only provide food and livelihood but also preserve the agricultural traditions and values that have been passed down from generation to generation.

festivals.title: Festivals
festivals.lede: The people of Reddivaripalli celebrate every festival together with devotion and happiness.

items.name: Sankranthi
items.note: Harvest festival celebrated with traditional games, rangoli, family gatherings, and cultural activities.

items.name: Ugadi
items.note: Telugu New Year celebrated with prayers, Ugadi Pachadi, and new beginnings.

items.name: Sri Rama Navami
items.note: Special prayers and celebrations dedicated to Lord Sri Rama.

items.name: Krishna Janmashtami
items.note: Celebrating the birth of Lord Krishna with devotional programs and cultural performances.

items.name: Varalakshmi Vratham
items.note: A sacred festival observed by women for the prosperity and well-being of their families.

items.name: Vinayaka Chavithi
items.note: Grand celebrations in honor of Lord Ganesha with community participation.

items.name: Dasara
items.note: Celebrating the victory of good over evil through cultural and religious events.

items.name: Deepavali
items.note: The Festival of Lights celebrated with prayers, lamps, and family gatherings.

items.name: Vana Pandaga
items.note: A unique tradition introduced by Sri G. Konda Reddy — villagers gather for two days to pray for timely rains, cook and eat together, and celebrate as one community.

items.name: Mathamma Jathara
items.note: The village gathers for Mathamma — drums, offerings, and shared faith.

items.name: Devapatlamma Jathara
items.note: Devotional celebrations for Sri Devapatlamma that bring families together in faith and community.

culturalEvents.title: Cultural Events
culturalEvents.lede: Reddivaripalli has always been known for its vibrant cultural programs and traditional village events. Many of these were introduced and encouraged by Sri G. Konda Reddy and continue to be celebrated today.

items.name: Mahabharata Natakam
items.note: Traditional stage performances depicting stories from the Mahabharata.

items.name: Kolla Pandem
items.note: Traditional rooster competitions enjoyed by the community.

items.name: Jallikattu
items.note: Traditional cattle-related sporting event celebrated with enthusiasm.

items.name: Cow Competitions
items.note: Celebrations that honor cattle and the farming life of the village.

items.name: Vana Bhojanalu
items.note: Community picnics where families gather to enjoy food, games, and togetherness in nature.

temples.title: Sacred Temples
temples.lede: The spiritual life of Reddivaripalli revolves around its ancient and respected temples, where villagers gather for worship and major religious celebrations.
temples.preservationIntro: Over the years, some of these historic temples have suffered damage due to age, natural deterioration, and unfortunate incidents. Today, the villagers remain committed to preserving this precious heritage for future generations.

items.name: Sri Ramalayam
items.note: One of the oldest temples in the village. According to village tradition, it was established during the time of Sri G. Konda Reddy. Due to its age, the structure has weakened considerably. Large tree roots have grown into the foundation and walls, causing significant damage. The villagers aspire to restore and preserve this temple so that future generations can continue to worship there.

items.name: Sri Shiva Temple
items.note: The ancient Sri Shiva Temple was once one of the village's most revered places of worship. The temple was destroyed, and the sacred Shiva Lingam and Nandi were found broken. Although the original structure no longer exists, the memory and spiritual significance continue to live in the hearts of the people. The villagers hope that one day this sacred temple will be restored.

items.name: Sri Mulasthanamma Temple
items.note: An important place of worship for the village. According to village tradition, it was established during the time of Sri G. Konda Reddy. Although it is currently in a stable condition, the community hopes to renovate and develop the temple in the future to preserve its heritage and provide improved facilities for devotees.

items.name: Sri Devapatlamma Temple
items.note: Recently reconstructed with the support and dedication of the villagers. Today, the temple stands in excellent condition and continues to serve as an important spiritual center where devotees gather for festivals and daily prayers.

items.name: Sri Mathamma Temple
items.note: A sacred place of devotion for Mathamma, where the village gathers in faith for prayers and Mathamma Jathara.

landmarks.title: Village Landmarks
landmarks.lede: Reddivaripalli is blessed with several important landmarks that represent its history, development, and community spirit.

items.name: Ragi Manu
items.note: At the entrance of Reddivaripalli stands the historic Ragi Manu, one of the village's most recognizable landmarks. For generations, it has welcomed visitors and served as a gathering place where villagers meet, discuss community matters, and celebrate together.

items.name: Village Kunta (Pond)
items.note: Located at the entrance of the village, the Kunta is an important natural resource. It has supported agriculture, livestock, and the daily lives of villagers for many years while adding to the beauty of the village.

items.name: Overhead Water Tank
items.note: Situated at the upper side of the village, ensuring a reliable supply of drinking water for the community.

items.name: Government Primary School
items.note: Located near the village entrance, the school has been educating generations of children and plays a vital role in building the future of Reddivaripalli.

items.name: Anganwadi Centre
items.note: Adjacent to the Primary School, supporting the health, nutrition, and early childhood education of young children while also providing care and guidance for mothers.

items.name: Gram Panchayat Office
items.note: Located near the Ragi Manu at the entrance of the village, serving as the administrative center where important village decisions are made and community welfare activities are coordinated.

items.name: Community Hall
items.note: Situated within the Panchayat Office premises, used for village meetings, social gatherings, awareness programs, celebrations, and community events.

items.name: Village Playground
items.note: A place where children and youth participate in sports, games, and recreational activities — especially during village festivals and annual events.

professionals.title: Education & Professionals
professionals.lede: Reddivaripalli takes great pride in its people — teachers, doctors, engineers, graduates, government servants, armed forces personnel, entrepreneurs, and artisans who carry the village's values into the wider world.

farmers.title: Farmers — The Backbone of Reddivaripalli
farmers.lede: Agriculture has always been the heart of our village. We proudly recognize the hardworking farmers whose dedication has sustained Reddivaripalli for generations.

memorial.title: In Loving Memory
memorial.lede: With deep respect and gratitude, the people of Reddivaripalli remember the great souls whose vision, leadership, hard work, and selfless service shaped our village. Though they are no longer with us, their legacy continues to live in every field, every festival, every temple, and in the hearts of every villager.

founder.name: Sri G. Konda Reddy
founder.bio: Founded the village around 1850 with the ideals of unity, equality, hospitality, and service. He welcomed every visitor with kindness, encouraged agriculture, introduced cultural programs, celebrated festivals with the entire community, organized Mahabharata Natakalu, Vana Pandaga, Kolla Pandem, and many traditional events, and laid the foundation for a peaceful and prosperous village. His vision continues to guide Reddivaripalli more than a century and a half later.

successor.name: Sri G. Venkata Subba Reddy
successor.bio: After Sri G. Konda Reddy, Sri G. Venkata Subba Reddy carried forward the founder's vision. As the respected village head and Panchayat leader, he upheld justice, resolved disputes with fairness, preserved village traditions, and ensured that the customs and celebrations established by his predecessor continued for future generations.

memorial.closing: Gone from our sight, but never from our hearts. Their legacy will continue to inspire every generation of Reddivaripalli.
memorial.legendsLede: Elders who shaped Reddivaripalli’s early generations.

vision.title: Our Vision
paragraphs: This website is dedicated to preserving the rich history, traditions, culture, agriculture, temples, and achievements of Reddivaripalli. It is a digital home for every villager — past, present, and future — connecting families across the world while honoring our ancestors and inspiring generations to come.
Dedicated with love and respect to every resident of Reddivaripalli who has contributed to the growth, unity, and prosperity of our beloved village.

about.title: About Reddivaripalli
paragraphs: Reddivaripalli — also known as Kondareddigaripalli — is a village rooted in unity, hospitality, agriculture, and faith. For more than 170 years it has stood as a place where families gather, traditions endure, and every guest is welcomed as one of our own.

Its historical significance reaches far beyond its fields: more than 32 surrounding villages once looked here for leadership, guidance, and peaceful resolution of community matters. That reputation for fairness and generosity remains central to our identity.

Culturally, Reddivaripalli is defined by shared festivals, temple traditions, agricultural seasons, and a deep respect for elders. Community values of equality, service, and togetherness continue to shape daily life and celebrations.
values: Unity across families and neighbouring villages
Hospitality — no guest leaves without care
Agriculture as livelihood and way of life
Respect for elders and service to society

origins.title: Origins of the Village
origins.lede: Founded around 1850 by Sri G. Konda Reddy of the Gundluru family — the beginning of Kondareddigaripalli, later known as Reddivaripalli.

timeline.title: Village founded
timeline.note: Sri G. Konda Reddy establishes Kondareddigaripalli with ideals of unity, dignity, and hospitality.

timeline.title: Regional leadership
timeline.note: The village becomes a centre for guidance and dispute resolution for more than 30 neighbouring villages.

timeline.title: Name evolves
timeline.note: Kondareddigaripalli comes to be proudly known as Reddivaripalli.

timeline.title: Living heritage
timeline.note: More than 170 years on, the founder’s values continue through festivals, agriculture, temples, and community service.

developmentJourney.title: Development Journey
developmentJourney.lede: From fertile fields and temple courtyards to roads, education, and a digital village home — Reddivaripalli continues to grow while honouring its roots.

milestones.title: Agriculture & livelihood
milestones.note: Generations of farmers built prosperity through grains, pulses, oilseeds, and hard work on fertile land.

milestones.title: Faith & public life
milestones.note: Temples, festivals, and Panchayat leadership strengthened social bonds and peaceful community order.

milestones.title: Education & professions
milestones.note: Sons and daughters of the village entered teaching, medicine, government service, engineering, and enterprise.

milestones.title: Infrastructure & schemes
milestones.note: Roads, water, and community works continue through Gram Panchayat initiatives and collective effort.
